messages:
alex-chen: Quick convo — leaning on a pattern for quiescent upgrades across Hosted / Dedicated / Private. TL;DR: propose a tiny upgrade-shim interface that handles in-flight KV cache migration, routing drain, and a telemetry flag so we can correlate before/after. Thoughts?

mei-k: love the idea. main risk is secrets/KMS handoff for Private installs — we can't pull keys into hosted shim. how do you imagine that?

alex-chen: good call. my thought: shim should be control-plane-light. It only coordinates signals (drain, migrate markers, trace-id propagation). Key material stays in runtime. For Private we call the customer's controlplane hook: `/v1/upgrade/ack` which returns a cert-signed token. For Hosted/Dedicated we mint a short-lived tmp token.

samir: hmm. any chance we avoid a custom hook for Private? Customers hate webhooks in air-gapped envs.

alex-chen: yeah — fallback plan: agent polls local socket for `upgrade.signal`. Agent-side binary handles KMS interaction and emits `upgrade.ready` file that shim watches. So two modes: webhook (cloud) or agent-signal (private).

mira: what about routing semantics? if we drain, do we fail fast or soft-fallback to a variant model (e.g., quantized)? Customers need continuity.

alex-chen: propose policy enum: `IMMEDIATE_FAIL`, `SOFT_FALLBACK`, `QUEUE_DRAIN`. Default for Hosted = `SOFT_FALLBACK` (route to compatible variant in same pool). Dedicated = `QUEUE_DRAIN` (respect capacity commitments). Private = customer-configurable, default `IMMEDIATE_FAIL` for strict isolation.

samir: sounds reasonable. need to document compatibility matrix for variants (kv cache layout, attention cache format). otherwise fallback can corrupt context.

alex-chen: absolutely — the shim will require a short capability handshake before fallback allowed. e.g.:

```
POST /v1/shim/handshake
{
  "model": "redwood-xxl-v1",
  "kv_format": "v2",
  "supports_cache_migration": true
}
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot posted: "canary deploy started for shim v0.3 on infra-staging" :information_source:

rohan: traces — how do we correlate pre/post traces? we need a stable trace-id across the switch so SLOs don't get split.

alex-chen: shim will inject `x-rw-shim-trace` header and mirror the original `traceparent` if present. Also emit a `upgrade.event` span to link. We'll add a dashboard that stitches traces by `x-rw-shim-session`.

mei-k: observability is great. also add a metric that counts fallback events per-customer per-hour so Optimize can suggest quantization or more capacity.

mira: ops question — if a Private customer rejects the handshake, what's the rollback story?

alex-chen: rollback = no commit. We keep old model running until explicit `upgrade.commit`. For in-place migrations we do copy-on-write for caches and only flip the pointer once migration finishes and `upgrade.commit` is issued. That gives an escape hatch.

samir: suggestion: force a max migration window and an emergency cutoff policy that auto-fallbacks to `IMMEDIATE_FAIL` if migration doesn't finish to avoid hanging traffic.

alex-chen: agreed. add `migration_timeout_seconds` and `emergency_policy`.

rohan: one more: telemetry privacy for Private customers — ensure shim logs are scrubbed and by default never leave the customer network.

alex-chen: yep — default logs are local. hosted/dedicated can opt-in to scrubbed telemetry export. we'll surface this in Console with clear toggle.

mira: ok this is actionable. next steps: 1) small RFC doc with sequence diagrams, 2) minimal handshake proto + HTTP shim spec, 3) agent-signal contract for Private. I'll take doc + sequence gif. alex want to own the handshake proto?

alex-chen: I'll draft the proto and a quick PoC shim. planning to open PR next week.

samir: FYI I'll add a compatibility test in infra-playbook to exercise kv conversions during CI.

ops-bot: note: meeting scheduled "Shim upgrade pattern sync" @channel tomorrow 10:30am in #architecture :calendar:

mei-k: thanks everyone. quick ack :thumbsup:
